finding.claim: Unauthenticated OS command injection via the `host` query parameter of GET /ping, which is concatenated into a string passed to child_process.exec.
finding.source: tools.js:6-7 req.query.host on the unauthenticated GET /ping route
finding.sink: tools.js:7 exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host, ...), which runs through /bin/sh -c

trace.note: app.get("/ping") route registered with no auth middleware
req.query.host concatenated into the shell command string without validation
exec spawns sh -c with the injected string, e.g. host=127.0.0.1;id

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, type check, allowlist, shell escaping, or execFile argv form on the path; no authentication or authorization middleware in tools.js; the fixed -c 1 flag does not constrain the host argument. Server listens on all interfaces at tools.js:28. Sibling routes /version (tools.js:16, execFile with constant argv) and /uptime (tools.js:25, constant command) take no user input and are SAFE.

verdict.guard_found: none. tools.js:6 registers app.get("/ping") with no auth middleware, and tools.js:7 concatenates req.query.host into the exec() string with no validation, escaping, or execFile argv form. tools.js:9 only handles the error case and does not gate the call. tools.js is the only file in the directory, so no upstream middleware or wrapper is present, and tools.js:28 calls app.listen(3001) without a host argument.
verdict.reason: The unauthenticated GET /ping route at tools.js:6 passes req.query.host unescaped into exec() at tools.js:7, which runs through /bin/sh -c, so an anonymous attacker can inject shell commands (e.g. host=127.0.0.1;id); the sibling /version and /uptime routes take no user input and are not affected.
